gen_risks.description: Mexican SMEs failing to adopt sustainability criteria face potential forward-exclusion from anchor company global and regional value chains.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated long-term green loans, SLLs, and technical assistance to help SMEs meet anchor company ESG and disclosure standards.
gen_risks.evidence: Firms that do not comply risk forward-exclusion from supply chains, with implications for sales and employment

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing in Sustainability-Linked Sub-loans if sustainability targets and indicators are insufficiently rigorous or unverified.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of Sustainability Plans, KPIs, and targets by qualified independent validation entities.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to, respectively, ex-ante validation and ex-post verification

gen_risks.description: Low market uptake and limited firm demand for sustainable financing instruments due to high transaction and certification costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Component 2 technical assistance to minimize transaction costs, support project preparation, and partner with anchor companies for outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: mitigate the risk of a situation where financing is available, but uptake is limited.

gen_risks.description: Participating financial institutions and firms lack technical capacity to appraise green investments and manage complex MRV requirements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver technical assistance, standardized templates, digital monitoring tools, and training to PFIs and firms under Component 2.
gen_risks.evidence: Key constraints go beyond tenor to include high Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) costs and limited capacity to structure, appraise and monitor investments.

gen_risks.description: Credit risk and borrower default on direct first-tier sub-loans and second-tier PFI on-lending exposures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce strict eligibility criteria, single-borrower exposure caps, credit risk margins, minimum co-financing, and standard NAFIN credit due diligence.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second-tier operations

gen_risks.description: Extreme climate events and hydro-meteorological hazards causing operational disruptions and loan delinquencies for SME/mid-cap borrowers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prioritize sub-projects that enhance operational climate resilience, water efficiency, and clean backup energy solutions.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms, as liquidity shortages and limited access to credit make it difficult

gen_risks.description: Foreign exchange rate volatility affecting balance sheet exposures or unhedged sub-borrowers.
gen_risks.mitigation: Manage balance sheet FX risk using domestic currency swaps and restrict USD-denominated sub-loans to firms with clear natural export hedges.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Persistent structural gender gaps in financial access limiting women-led businesses from accessing project-supported loan instruments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish transparent access criteria, gender-focused communication campaigns, and dedicated intermediate results tracking for women-inclusive enterprises.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico has a 14 percent gender gap in financial access... women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing

gen_risks.description: Procurement implementation delays arising from NAFIN staff's lack of direct experience conducting World Bank selection processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Assign a dedicated qualified procurement professional to the project and provide hands-on training and close supervision from World Bank procurement specialists.
gen_risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

gen_risks.description: Financial management efficiency constraints and reporting delays due to reliance on legacy IT systems requiring manual data consolidation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish formal reconciliation procedures, supervisory review workflows, targeted internal audit coverage, and explicit POM financial reporting protocols.
gen_risks.evidence: efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

gen_risks.description: Substantial Environmental and Social (E&S) risks associated with financial intermediary sub-loan portfolios.
gen_risks.mitigation: Apply NAFIN's ESMS and PFI due diligence, enforce a ring-fenced Exclusion List, and conduct periodic World Bank sample audits of sub-projects.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social Risk Classification Substantial

gen_risks.description: High industrial fossil fuel dependence and energy intensity exposing target enterprises to transition risks and energy price spikes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Target sub-loan allocations to energy efficiency, renewable energy scale-up, and decarbonization investments aligned with Mexico's Sustainable Taxonomy.
gen_risks.evidence: This combination of fossil fuels and energy intensity means that firms are exposed to both energy-transition risks and high energy costs.

gen_risks.description: Implementation friction and delay due to novel market application of Sustainability-Linked Loans in the Mexican financial system.
gen_risks.mitigation: Upgrade NAFIN's Sustainable Finance Framework, pilot SLLs in first-tier operations before scaling to second-tier PFIs, and provide extensive capacity building.
gen_risks.evidence: While the Project represents the first systematic application of Sustainability Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) debt instruments in Mexico's financial system

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
